title: Real-time communication with WebSockets

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
FastAPI builds JSON APIs that web and mobile applications call over HTTP; type annotations help validate inputs and describe the API contract.
PURPOSE AND REAL-WORLD USE

A normal HTTP request ends with its response; a WebSocket keeps a connection open for two-way messages. A FastAPI endpoint accepts, reads, and replies. This is an echo server; a browser client uses the WebSocket API.

To run these examples locally, install `pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx` plus any extra package named in the lesson. Save the server example as `app.py` and start `uvicorn app:app --reload`. `--reload` is for development only.

WHERE DOES THIS APPEAR IN REAL LIFE?
A chat, shared board, or game room can push new events to a client immediately.
If this part is omitted: Polling repeatedly for updates adds delay and traffic; WebSocket uses an open connection.

LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect` — Imports a required type or tool; without it, the name is unavailable.
`app = FastAPI()` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`@app.websocket("/ws")` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`async def websocket_echo(websocket: WebSocket):` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`await websocket.accept()` — Waits for an asynchronous I/O operation; without `await`, the value may only be a coroutine.
`try:` — Continues the application's data handling or control flow.
`while True:` — Continues the application's data handling or control flow.
`message = await websocket.receive_text()` — Waits for an asynchronous I/O operation; without `await`, the value may only be a coroutine.
`await websocket.send_text(f"Echo: {message}")` — Waits for an asynchronous I/O operation; without `await`, the value may only be a coroutine.
`except WebSocketDisconnect:` — Continues the application's data handling or control flow.
`return` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.
PRACTICE: CHECK IT WITH AN HTTP CLIENT
This complete file calls the app locally with TestClient; it does not open a server port. Install `httpx` for TestClient.
COMPLETE RUNNABLE CLIENT TEST
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect

app = FastAPI()

@app.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_echo(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    try:
        while True:
            message = await websocket.receive_text()
            await websocket.send_text(f"Echo: {message}")
    except WebSocketDisconnect:
        return

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

with TestClient(app) as client:
    with client.websocket_connect("/ws") as socket:
        socket.send_text("hello")
        reply = socket.receive_text()
print(reply)

COMMON MISTAKES
Treating WebSocket like a normal GET and ignoring disconnects; connections can drop, so handle cleanup.

spans.title: Practical tip
spans.text: Run the server, then use `new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:8000/ws')` in a browser console and try `send()` and `onmessage`.

spans.title: One level deeper
spans.text: WebSocket connections consume server memory and file descriptors; plan connection limits and fan-out for many clients.

spans.title: Important warning
spans.text: Add origin checks, authentication, message-size limits, and connection-rate limits in production.
